analysis.title: Using options to add defensive upside to the European AI Ecosystem
key_insights: UBS European Equity Strategist Gerry Fowler is bullish on the 'second phase of industrial acceleration'. This is the supply-side catch-up trade: spending to build enough capacity to meet equipment and materials demand from the AI build-out.
Fowler's key Buy-rated list for the theme: Siemens, ASML, Schneider Electric, Anglo American, Air Liquide, VAT Group, Comet, Inficon and SPIE. The full tiered list is in fig 3 of his note.

Industrials analyst Andre Kukhnin says European Industrials now imply value after October's AI-related correction. On average, Electricals price about 160bps lower mid-cycle growth than on 2 October (reverse DCF).
Within electrification, Nexans, Schneider, Siemens Energy and Prysmian were hit hardest since the start-of-October peak, and the report says they now price in '½ of less growth' vs that peak.
Q3 reporting so far supports fundamental momentum. Schneider's organic sales growth was 16.9% vs consensus 13.9% and UBS upgraded forecasts. ASML pointed to a strong backlog and UBS raised numbers.
Air Liquide reported strong pricing and a small topline beat. VAT Group and Comet orders were strong enough to point to upside pressure on consensus. Inficon beat and raised with record orders.
Nexans beat on its grid and copper sales businesses. Prysmian's electrification division drove its beat and raise.

US hyperscaler results remain supportive. META tightened FY26 capex guidance toward the top end. Alphabet was weak after hours mainly on search weakness and held capex guidance. A little uncertainty on 2027 makes options on suppliers the preferred route.
UBS Systematic Advisory data shows investors quickly returning to the AI Industrials trade (UBXEAIIN) as the sector started reporting Q3.

UBS Derivatives Strategist Kieran Diamond proposes five upside structures into year-end: call-spreads on ASML, Schneider Electric and Air Liquide, and call-spread collars (call spreads funded by selling puts) on Siemens Energy and Anglo American.

At the index level, the UBS AI Industrials basket correlates 0.8-0.9 with the SXNP index. The basket has more electrification weight, includes data-centre construction names such as ACS, and has no defence exposure, which is a large feature of SXNP.
Realised vol is cheaper for SXNP, so UBS priced a call-spread on the Stoxx Europe 600 Industrial Goods & Services index. Pricing on the specific AI Industrials basket is available on request.
